metadata.title: Dubai Real Estate Investment Report 2026 · Forecasts & Trends · ShanGroup
metadata.description: 112-page institutional research report on Dubai property market 2026: price forecasts, segment breakdown, top districts, macro drivers, risks. Free PDF on request.

hero.subtitle: 112 pages of forecasts, segment data and district-level analysis — distilled from $2.4B of transactions and 38 institutional sources. Built for investors, family offices and senior bankers.

highlights.subtitle: What we'd tell a board in 60 seconds. Each conclusion has 8–14 pages of supporting evidence in the full report.

items.n: Range: +5.8% (bear) to +12.1% (bull). Driven by population + Golden Visa demand.
Up from 98K in 2025. Off-plan retains ~58% share. Secondary recovers H2.
Russian, Indian and British buyers still top-3. UK share rising on tax pressure.
Mid-market apartments. Premium villas: 4.2%. Short-let / Airbnb: 8–10%.
5-year peak. Mid-market absorbed in ≤ 9 months. Watch oversupply in JVT, DSO.
Property-backed +42% YoY. We forecast 180K+ in 2026 as thresholds stabilise.

marketSize.subtitle: The total addressable market — sized for comparison against London, Singapore and Miami in the full report.

segments.subtitle: Market share of transaction value by asset type — and our 2026 outlook for each. Premium villas continue to lead growth; mid-apartments lead volume.

items.label: Apartments
items.outlook: Volume engine. Off-plan + ready balance. Mid-segment ($300–800K) absorbed fastest.

items.label: Villas & townhouses
items.outlook: Premium villas lead capital growth. Family-led demand from Golden Visa relocations.

items.label: Penthouses
items.outlook: Limited supply on Palm, Downtown, Bluewaters. Resale liquidity strongest at $5M+.

items.label: Waterfront / branded
items.outlook: Branded residences (Ritz-Carlton, Bulgari, Armani) outperforming standard luxury by ~3%.

segments.footnote: * Transaction value share, DLD 2025 actuals. Growth and yield are 2026 base-case forecasts. Branded residence sample is judgement-weighted.

forecast.subtitle: Indexed price growth 2024 = 100. Three scenarios. The bear path assumes a 2027 oversupply correction; the bull path assumes Golden Visa volumes hold above 200K/year.
forecast.footnote: * Index method — Property Monitor citywide weighted by transaction volume. ShanGroup base case 60%, bull 25%, bear 15% probability weighting.

hotDistricts.subtitle: Where the Q2 2026 fundamentals diverge most from current pricing. Detailed write-ups (12–18 pages each) are in the full report.

items.name: Dubai Creek Harbour
items.thesis: New CBD around the Burj-class tower. Off-plan deliveries 2026–2028 line up with infrastructure unlocking.

items.name: Sobha Hartland II
items.thesis: Premium waterfront with the city's highest forecast capital growth. Sobha brand carries resale premium.

items.name: Jumeirah Village Circle
items.thesis: Anomalously high net yield (7.2%) at $320K entry. Volume-rental thesis for cashflow investors.

items.name: MBR City
items.thesis: EMAAR / Sobha / MAG master-plan maturing. Green infrastructure and metro extensions are the catalyst.

items.name: Palm Jebel Ali
items.thesis: Sister-Palm relaunch. Long-dated thesis (delivery 2028+) for capital-growth investors. Supply discipline strong.

items.title: Population +5.2%/year
items.body: Dubai population now 3.85M. Inbound is professional and family, not transient — sustains end-user housing demand.

items.title: Golden Visa programme
items.body: Property threshold stabilised at AED 2M ($545K). 138K visas issued 2025 — half property-backed. Demand floor is policy-set.

items.title: Tourism 20M target
items.body: Government Tourism Strategy 2031: 25M arrivals. Short-let yields 8–10% in tourist districts (Marina, Downtown, JBR).

items.title: Zero personal tax
items.body: 0% personal income tax, 0% capital gains, 0% inheritance. Combined with 137 DTAs — UAE remains uniquely tax-efficient.

items.title: Corporate diversification
items.body: Non-oil GDP 73% in 2025. DIFC + ADGM moving up FT financial-centre rankings. Financial services demand drives premium rentals.

items.title: Regulator credibility
items.body: DLD, RERA and FTA reforms 2023–2025 strengthened transparency. Buyer protections rival London / Singapore.

risks.subtitle: Every report says 'risks exist'. We rate, size and stress-test them. Here are the top three from our risk register.

items.title: Oversupply 2027–2028
items.body: 47K units in 2026, 52K projected 2027. Mid-market absorption is fine; risk concentrates in commodity off-plan (JVT, DSO). Premium and prime segments insulated.
items.stress: Bear-case forecast prices in a 6–8% correction in commodity segments. Premium remains positive.

items.title: Global recession & rates
items.body: GCC pegged to USD — UAE rates follow Fed. If higher-for-longer extends into late 2026, mortgage volumes soften, cash share rises further.
items.stress: Historical: cash share 73% in 2024. Demand floor holds; transaction mix shifts towards end-user / family-office cash.

items.title: Regional geopolitics
items.body: Regional escalations historically *increase* Dubai inflows (safe-haven trade). Tail risk: direct UAE involvement — low base rate, but cannot be priced out.
items.stress: Stress event 2024 saw inflows accelerate, not fall. We monitor and disclose positioning quarterly.

methodology.subtitle: Same rigour you'd expect from an institutional research desk — peer-reviewed before publication. We disclose the model assumptions so you can dispute them.

items.d: DLD transactions (full year), Property Monitor, Bayut, FTA, Dubai Statistics Centre, Knight Frank, JLL, CBRE, Savills.
$2.4B of transaction data referenced. 38 institutional sources cited. 312 ShanGroup client transactions cross-checked.
Three-scenario Monte Carlo with weighted probability. Index price by transaction volume, not asking. Service charges modelled separately.
Reviewed pre-publication by two independent UAE-licensed valuers and one academic economist. Notes on dissent included in appendix.
Quarterly mini-updates (12–16 pp) free to report recipients. Next update: end Q3 2026.
ShanGroup transacts in this market. We disclose our positioning by segment in the appendix. No paid placements.

Data cut-off is Q2 2026 (March 31). Quarterly updates follow. The PDF you receive will always be the most recent annual edition; mini-updates are sent by email.
Yes, with attribution: 'ShanGroup, Dubai Real Estate Investment Report 2026, Edition 04'. Email us for the higher-resolution chart pack.
Forecasts are wrong individually. Scenarios force the reader to think in distributions and pre-commit to actions on each path — that's what institutional research is supposed to enable.
No. It's our marketing — we sell brokerage and investment advisory. The honest version of that exchange is: we give you world-class data, you remember us when you're ready to transact.
